title: Witnessed flat models and compactification domains for finite reduction
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-sf-datum]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p$, $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $B=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$ for $1\le m\le n$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Use ordinary constant-ring module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], their exact comparison inverse images $\nu_T^*$ [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], and bounded constructibility and Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ have Tor amplitudes $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$.

There exist bounded flat constructible etale complexes $P$ on $X$ and $Q$ on $Y$, zero outside $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$, together with isomorphisms $\nu_X^*P\simeq K$ and $\nu_Y^*Q\simeq L$. Here flat means tensoring module sheaves with the term is exact, and constructible means locally constant with finite module values on a finite locally closed constructible stratification. Write $P_A=P$, $Q_A=Q$, $P_B=P\otimes_A B$, and $Q_B=Q\otimes_A B$ termwise. For $R=A,B$, these are bounded flat constructible $R$-complexes with the same respective degree bounds, representing etale origins of $K_R,L_R$, where $K_A=K$, $L_A=L$ and $K_B=K\otimes_A^LB$, $L_B=L\otimes_A^LB$ with their $B$-actions. The signed total tensor $\operatorname{Tot}(P_R\otimes_R f^{-1}Q_R)$ represents an etale origin of $H_R=K_R\otimes_R^L Lf_R^*L_R$ and is flat constructible, zero outside $[a+c,b+d]$. In particular $K_R,L_R,H_R$ lie in their bounded constructible finite-Tor categories with those bounds, and these comparison isomorphisms are etale-origin witnesses.

The morphism $f$ admits a compactification [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For every compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\bar X\xrightarrow{r}Y$, $rj=f$, with $j$ open and $r$ proper, and for either coefficient ring, $j_{!,R}K_R$ and $j_{!,R}H_R$ have bounded constructible etale origins and the respective Tor bounds $[a,b]$ and $[a+c,b+d]$. Under the canonical open tensor isomorphism [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula], $j_{!,R}H_R\simeq j_{!,R}K_R\otimes_R^L Lr_R^*L_R$. Thus both proper-factor inputs have the required witnessed finite-Tor domains.

proof.text: The coefficient rings and quotient map are the existing Coeff, finiteCoeff and quotient constructions. Apply the Mathlib finite-type-over-Noetherian instances to the structure maps of X and Y, obtaining IsNoetherian on both schemes. Nagata supplies a compactification of f. No ambient compactification scheme needs a Noetherian or finite-type hypothesis in the fixed-module open-extension argument below.

The native fixed-ModuleCat constructibleFiniteTor hypothesis is, by definition, bounded etale origin together with finite Tor amplitude. Unpack its bounded etale origin and isomorphism. The source fixed-module Tor comparison torAmplitudeIn_mapDerivedCategory_iff reflects the prescribed interval along that isomorphism. Convert source constructibility to finite constant-value constructibility using isConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf_iff_isConstructibleSheaf, and express boundedness by the interval [min a b,max a b] of its t-structure bounds. Apply hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_exists_finiteValueConstructibleModel in the prescribed interval. Composing its localized model isomorphism with the origin isomorphism constructs P and Q. Thus no intrinsic-realization equivalence or new choice of inverse functor is needed.

For any flat constructible model P, use boundedFlatCoefficientSiteSquare to obtain flatness and the same support interval for its termwise coefficient reduction. constructibleCoefficientSiteSquare gives finite-value constructibility of the same reduced terms, including its proved empty-scheme normalization. Construct the reduced origin isomorphism explicitly as N_B[P_B] -> [N_B P_B] -> [(N_A P)_B] -> T_B[N_A P] -> T_B K. The first and last comparisons are exact localization factors; the middle chain comparison is the square theorem’s B-linear chainComparison; the third arrow is the inverse of the scalarExtensionRepresentative whose invertibility is supplied by boundedFlatCoefficientSiteSquare. This retains the B-action and uses no flatness of B over A.

For any finite coefficient ring R and model Q on Y, apply the source etale upperStarPreservesFlat instance termwise; categorical flatness is equivalent here to exact tensorRight via braiding. Source constructible pullback and the finite-value/source constructibility comparison give constructibility of each pullback term. Exact inverse image preserves zero terms, giving the same support interval. The exact-functor localization factor and mapDerivedCategoryComparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso identify this pulled-back model’s comparison image with G.mapDerivedCategory(L). The canonical leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory for exact constant-coefficient pro-etale inverse image identifies this with Lf^*L. These are the fixed-module specializations of the comparison and exactness lemmas, without the unnecessary line tensor and shift. The etale flat-pullback instance is proved by the geometric-fiber flatness criterion; the fixed-scalar pro-etale flat-pullback instance provides the recorded derived-pullback API.

Apply finiteFlatConstructible_totalTensor to P and the termwise pullback of Q, with T equal to the actual signed mapBifunctor defining total. Its first three conclusions give the required model in [a+c,b+d]. Map its localized total-to-derived-tensor isomorphism through exact comparison, then use the source derivedTensorObjCompMapDerivedCategoryComparisonUpperStarIso, the fixed-module specialization of the ringed-topos tensor comparison. Substitute the two origin isomorphisms and the pullback isomorphism of the previous step. This gives exactly origin(total) isomorphic to tensorInput. A bounded flat constructible model gives source bounded constructibility and the full universal Tor test by constructibleFiniteTor_Q_obj and torAmplitudeIn_Q_obj_of_flat. Exact comparison preserves both, and transport along the model isomorphism gives the three constructibleFiniteTor and exact-interval clauses. Unpacking bounded etale origin and converting constructibility gives each explicitly witnessedDomain.

For each compactification, its open immersion is quasi-compact because its source X is Noetherian. For any witnessed input, unpack a bounded etale origin O. Reflect its exact Tor interval through the source fixed-module Tor comparison. The source theorem boundedConstructible_and_torAmplitudeIn_mapDerivedCategory_openImmersionLowerShriek preserves bounded constructibility and precisely that interval, using the cohomological bound implied by the Tor bound. The canonical mapDerivedCategoryOpenImmersionLowerShriekComparisonUpperStarIso followed by extension of the original origin isomorphism identifies comparison(j_! O) with j_! K. Transport bounded constructibility and the universal Tor test through this isomorphism; its etale origin supplies the required witness. Apply this argument to K and tensorInput at both coefficient levels. No property of the ambient scheme beyond being the target of this quasi-compact open immersion is needed.

The existing real-data definition openTensorIso is retained verbatim. It first maps the canonical congruence and derived pullback composition isomorphisms through tensor by K and open extension, and then applies derivedOpenImmersionLowerShriekProjectionIso. It therefore identifies the second witnessed proper-factor input with j_!K tensor Lr^*L for the same chosen compactification, exactly as required. Finally apply the uniform stage_of_models argument to P,Q and to their same chosen termwise coefficient reductions, and pair these two stages with Nagata compactification existence.
